statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-14662 (PostgreSQL tsvector and tsquery undersize allocations, via integer wraparound) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 16.15 on the 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14662/ lists 16.15 as the fixed release for major version 16, the 16.15 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.15/, list this CVE, and the fix is commits https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/23d9ad771817c123ebdc16ebc65977754c82b5ab and https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/90649b6f846c7593f0f57b2b821b8d8eb1e18693 (changing the tsvector and tsquery code under src/backend/tsearch and src/backend/utils/adt, each tagged Security: CVE-2026-14662 and back-patched through 14). Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD on the 3.23-stable branch lists CVE-2026-14662 under its 16.15-r0 secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball and applies no security backports, and the postgres server binary in each published build reports its upstream release on both x86_64 and aarch64: 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 report PostgreSQL 16.15 and 16.16 and carry the fix, while the earlier published builds 16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0 report 16.13 and 16.14 and are affected. 16.15-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

CVE-2026-14662 (PostgreSQL tsvector and tsquery undersize allocations, via integer wraparound) affects PostgreSQL 18 before 18.6 and is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 18.6: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14662/ and the 18.6 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/. PostgreSQL 18.5 was never released (the 18.6 release notes say so), so although Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD on the 3.23-stable branch lists CVE-2026-14662 under an 18.5-r0 secfixes entry, the first DHI postgresql18 build that carries the fix is 18.6-r0: https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql18 18.6-r0 package for Alpine 3.23 is the upgrade to 18.6, and its postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 18.6 on both x86_64 and aarch64. The earlier published DHI builds for Alpine 3.23 (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0 and 18.4-r0) are upstream releases before 18.6 and their server binaries report those versions, so they are affected; 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 carry the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-14662, integer wraparound in tsvector and tsquery functions that undersizes an allocation and writes out of bounds, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14662/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-14662. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
